candidate_relations.reason: Both are primary bone/soft-tissue sarcomas that can arise in young patients and cause lytic vertebral destruction, but Ewing sarcoma and giant cell-rich osteosarcoma are histologically and biologically distinct diagnoses. The reference requires osteosarcoma with giant cell-rich subtype; Ewing sarcoma is an incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Ewing sarcoma is a distinct primary bone/soft-tissue malignancy; shares some features (lytic vertebral destruction, young patient, large mass) but is a different histological entity from giant cell-rich osteosarcoma

candidate_relations.label: Lymphoma, mediastinal
candidate_relations.reason: Although the clinical team considered hematologic malignancy given atypical imaging, mediastinal lymphoma does not explain the lytic T1-T2 vertebral destruction with cortical fracture characteristic of osteosarcoma, and is a fundamentally different diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Mediastinal lymphoma is a hematologic malignancy; does not account for lytic vertebral cortical destruction or the osteosarcoma histology required by the reference

case_quality_flags: Giant cell-rich osteosarcoma arising from thoracic inlet/pleura with vertebral involvement is extremely rare; differential is broad and histologic confirmation is required
Both candidates were plausible pre-biopsy differentials but neither matches the reference diagnosis
